section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Vector Concept
section_1.content: Define a vector as a directed line segment from the origin. Visualize 2D vectors as arrows. Introduce 'Linear Combination' as scaling and adding arrows together.
section_1.example: Imagine a robot arm moving in a 2D plane: scaling two basic motor inputs (v1, v2) to reach any coordinate (x, y).

section_2.title: The Concept of Span: 'Reachability'
section_2.content: Define Span as the set of all possible points reachable by taking linear combinations of a set of vectors. Visualize this as the 'shadow' or 'area' cast by the vectors.
section_2.example: Two non-parallel vectors in 2D 'span' the entire plane; one vector only spans a single line.

section_3.title: Linear Dependence: The 'Redundant' Vector
section_3.content: Explain Linear Dependence: A set is dependent if one vector can be expressed as a combination of others (i.e., it doesn't add 'new' dimensions). Visualize this as a third vector lying flat on the plane formed by the first two.
section_3.example: If you have three people pulling a wagon in the same direction, the third person is 'linearly dependent'—their effort doesn't change the path.

section_4.title: Bases: The Minimalist Framework
section_4.content: Define a Basis as the 'Goldilocks' set: enough vectors to span the space, but no redundancy (linearly independent). This acts as a coordinate system for the space.
section_4.example: The standard basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) are the most efficient 'map' for a 2D grid.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap the logical progression: Linear Combinations build Span; too many vectors create Dependence; the minimal set required to span is a Basis.
section_5.example: Think of a basis as the 'keys' on a piano: they are independent notes that, when combined, can span the entire musical range of the instrument.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.5 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
